full_text_en:
Gansu Huayuan Industrial Co., Ltd. et al. v. Lanzhou Bank Co., Ltd. Qingyang Branch et al. — dispute over a financial loan contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where a party brings multiple claims based on multiple legal relationships, and although there is some de facto connection between those relationships, the claims are not based on the same facts or the subject matter of the action is not the same or of the same type, and after the people's court has provided clarification, the party still refuses to file separate lawsuits, the court may rule to dismiss the action.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling

(2019) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 77

Appellants (Plaintiffs at First Instance): Gansu Huayuan Industrial Co., Ltd. Domicile: 17-18/F, Huayuan Holiday Tourism Hotel, South Side of Qinghua West Road and East Side of Changqing South Road, Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Zhifeng, General Manager of the Company.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Qingyang Teheng Operation Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 150 Changqing South Road, Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Bian Runmei, Executive Director of the Company.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Qingyang Teheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 1011, Building 2, No. 8 Shuozhou West Road, Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Qin Kunyu, Executive Director and Manager of the Company.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Qin Kunyu, male, born November 28, 1973, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Bian Runmei, female, born December 18, 1950, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Ding Yiwen, female, born June 20, 1980, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Jointly Authorized Agent ad litem of the above six appellants: Zhou Wanfa, Attorney at Gansu Longjian Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Lanzhou Bank Co., Ltd. Qingyang Branch. Domicile: No. 66 Changqing North Road, Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Person in Charge: Xing Yuejun, Branch Manager.

Authorized Agent ad litem: Guo Jun, female, Assistant Branch Manager and Manager of the Customer Manager Department.

Authorized Agent ad litem: Yin Jiye, Attorney at Gansu Da'ercheng Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Liu Xingwei, male, born March 20, 1971, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Weiyang District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Qingyang Chunyuan Fruit and Vegetable Warehouse Co., Ltd. Domicile: Qijialou Village, Wenquan Township, Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Mi Chunhui, General Manager of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Qingyang Haowei Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Lanzhou East Road (opposite Dongshu Yipin), Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Li Ning, Chairperson of the Board of the Company.

Authorized Agent ad litem: Wan Penghui, male, employee of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Gansu Ruixinyuan Import and Export Trade Co., Ltd. Domicile: Zhongqing Fortune Plaza, No. 538 South Street, Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Wannian, Executive Director and General Manager of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Gansu Hongda Road and Bridge Construction Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 12 Guxiang West Road, Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Wei Zhenggang, Executive Director of the Company.

Authorized Agent ad litem: Zhai Haowen, male, Legal Counsel of the Company.

Third Party at First Instance: Gansu Longdong Automobile Transportation Co., Ltd. Domicile: North Section of West Ring Road, Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yixiong, Manager of the Company.

Authorized Agent ad litem: Liu Xingwei, male, Shareholder of the Company.

Third Party at First Instance: Wei Zhenggang, male, born July 14, 1969, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Huachi County, Gansu Province.

Third Party at First Instance: Li Ning, male, born January 3, 1980, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Qingcheng County, Gansu Province.

Authorized Agent ad litem: Wan Penghui, male, born November 18, 1975, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Ning County, Gansu Province.

Third Party at First Instance: Liu Wannian, male, born May 20, 1979, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Xifeng District, Qingyang City, Gansu Province.

The appellants, Gansu Huayuan Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huayuan Company), Qingyang Teheng Operation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Teheng Operation Company), Qingyang Teheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Teheng Real Estate Company), Qin Kunyu, Bian Runmei, and Ding Yiwen, appealed against the civil ruling (2018) Gan Min Chu No. 136 of the Gansu High People's Court in the case concerning a dispute over a financial loan contract with the respondents, Lanzhou Bank Co., Ltd. Qingyang Branch (hereinafter referred to as Lanzhou Bank), Liu Xingwei, Qingyang Chunyuan Fruit and Vegetable Warehouse Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chunyuan Company), Qingyang Haowei Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haowei Company), Gansu Ruixinyuan Import and Export Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ruixinyuan Company), Gansu Hongda Road and Bridge Construction Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongda Company), and the third parties at first instance, Gansu Longdong Automobile Transportation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longdong Company), Wei Zhenggang, Li Ning, and Liu Wannian. After the case was docketed on January 15, 2019, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and tried the case. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

Huayuan Company, Teheng Operation Company, Teheng Real Estate Company, Qin Kunyu, Bian Runmei, and Ding Yiwen (hereinafter referred to as the six persons including Huayuan Company) filed the following appeal requests: 1. Set aside the first-instance ruling; 2. Direct the first-instance court to conduct substantive trial of this case; 3. Litigation costs at both the first instance and on appeal shall be borne by the respondents and the third parties. Facts and reasons: The basic facts of this case contain three parts: First, the "mortgage package agreement" centered on Huayuan Company providing a mortgage over real property, whereby Longdong Company borrowed money from Lanzhou Bank, Longdong Company repaid the loan on behalf of 21 fruit farmers, Lanzhou Bank promised to later lend money to Huayuan Company and Longdong Company, and Liu Xingwei and Chunyuan Company provided counter-guarantee commitments to Huayuan Company; Second, the "repayment package agreement" centered on Teheng Operation Company repaying the loan to Lanzhou Bank on behalf of Longdong Company, whereby Lanzhou Bank lent money to Teheng Operation Company, Haowei Company, Hongda Company, Ruixinyuan Company, Teheng Real Estate Company, Wei Zhenggang, Li Ning, Liu Wannian, Qin Kunyu, Bian Runmei, and Ding Yiwen provided guarantees for Teheng Operation Company, Qin Kunyu pledged his company equity to Haowei Company, Hongda Company, and Ruixinyuan Company as a counter-guarantee, and Lanzhou Bank released the mortgage on Huayuan Company's real property. These two "package agreements" in turn contain several contracts of different natures. Third, the facts of the damages claim for compensation arising from the loan-mortgage-guarantee relationship, whereby the other party's breach of contract and tort prevented Huayuan Company from obtaining financing, causing losses from the suspension of its development project and interest losses. The above facts constitute a complete "factual situation of a loan-mortgage-guarantee and damages claim". The disputes in this case include a dispute over the rescission of the "repayment package agreement", a dispute over the rescission of the "mortgage package agreement", and a dispute over damages. Although the specific facts underlying each dispute and each claim are different, the contracts are of different natures, the specific legal relationships are different, and the nature of the claims is also different, they are causally connected and closely related, arising from the same facts and are inseparable. Pursuant to Article 221 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Judicial Interpretation on Civil Procedure Law), where a dispute arises from the same facts and the parties file separate lawsuits with the same people's court, the court may consolidate the trials. Accordingly, the first-instance ruling dismissing the action of the six persons including Huayuan Company was an error in the application of the law and should be set aside.

Lanzhou Bank argued that the action brought by the six persons including Huayuan Company was not a dispute arising from indivisible facts, that the action was not a necessary joint action, and that there was no legal causal relationship between the three groups of facts on which the action was based, so the actions should not be consolidated. Lanzhou Bank requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original ruling affirmed.

Liu Xingwei argued that he respected the court's opinion, that each claim in this case should be litigated separately, and that they should not be combined in one action.

Chunyuan Company argued that the appeal should be dismissed and the original ruling affirmed.

Haowei Company argued that the appeal should be dismissed and the original ruling affirmed.

Ruixinyuan Company did not appear to defend.

Hongqiao Company argued that the appeal should be dismissed and the original ruling affirmed.

Longdong Company submitted an opinion agreeing with the opinion of the first-instance court.

Wei Zhenggang did not appear to submit an opinion.

Li Ning submitted an opinion agreeing with the opinion of the first-instance court.

Liu Wannian did not appear to submit an opinion.

The six persons including Huayuan Company filed the following claims with the first-instance court: 1. Rescind the repayment by Teheng Operation Company on behalf of Longdong Company of the amount of RMB 36,488,949.99 owed to Lanzhou Bank, and order Lanzhou Bank to return the said repayment to Teheng Operation Company; 2. Rescind the loan contract under which Teheng Operation Company borrowed RMB 23 million from Lanzhou Bank, and concurrently rescind the guarantee contracts concluded between Teheng Real Estate Company, Qin Kunyu, Ding Yiwen, and Bian Runmei with Lanzhou Bank for the said loan, and confirm that after the rescission of the said contracts, Teheng Operation Company shall return the loan of RMB 23 million to Lanzhou Bank; 3. Rescind the pledge contracts and the registration of pledges under which Qin Kunyu pledged 100% of the equity in Teheng Real Estate Company valued at RMB 33.6 million (with each pledge of RMB 11.2 million) to Haowei Company, Ruixinyuan Company, and Hongda Company; 4. Rescind the letter of commitment issued by Qin Kunyu stating that "no reporting, accusation, or other means of recourse shall be pursued against Xiao Fei"; 5. Rescind the mortgage contract and the mortgage registration concluded between Huayuan Company and Lanzhou Bank as security for Longdong Company's loan of RMB 30 million from Lanzhou Bank; 6. Order Lanzhou Bank, Chunyuan Company, and Liu Xingwei to jointly compensate Huayuan Company for the interest losses (calculated at 6% per annum from the date of repayment on September 28, 2017 until the date the said repayment is rescinded and Lanzhou Bank fully refunds the amount) arising from Huayuan Company's self-financing of RMB 13,488,949.99 to repay the loan owed by Longdong Company to Lanzhou Bank, tentatively calculated as of June 28, 2018, amounting to RMB 607,002.75, and to bear joint and several liability for compensation; 7. Order Lanzhou Bank, Chunyuan Company, and Liu Xingwei to jointly compensate Huayuan Company for the loss of income from the mortgage of the "Huayuan Holiday Tourism Hotel" (calculated at 3% of RMB 150 million for the period from December 30, 2015 to September 30, 2017) amounting to RMB 7,875,000, and to bear joint and several liability for compensation; 8. Order Lanzhou Bank, Chunyuan Company, and Liu Xingwei to jointly compensate Teheng Real Estate Company for various losses (including lost profits) tentatively calculated at RMB 80 million arising from the suspension of construction of the "Xinhewan" commercial and residential community project from March 1, 2016 to September 30, 2017 due to the funding gap; 9. Order Liu Xingwei to guarantee the debts in this case with all his property rights and interests in the contractual operation of the "Huayuan Holiday Tourism Hotel", including the rescission of the operation contract, and with all his personal property rights and interests such as the RMB 5 million operation fee already paid, RMB 1 million decoration deposit, and initial decoration investments; 10. Order Lanzhou Bank, Chunyuan Company, and Liu Xingwei to bear all litigation costs of this case.

Facts and reasons: On September 30, 2014, Lanzhou Bank granted a loan of RMB 30 million to 21 fruit farmers including Ren Guilong, with Chunyuan Company providing a mortgage over its fruit warehouse as security, for a term of one year. The said loan was not actually disbursed to the 21 fruit farmers, but was actually controlled by Chunyuan Company and on-lent to others at high interest for profit. After the loan fell due, because Chunyuan Company was unable to repay on time, Lanzhou Bank hoped that Chunyuan Company would resolve the matter quickly by "rolling over the debt with a new loan". In or around November 2015, Mi Chunhui, the legal representative of Chunyuan Company, found Liu Xingwei, the controlling shareholder of Longdong Company, who had creditor-debtor relationships with him, to discuss the matter. Xiao Fei, the person in charge of Lanzhou Bank, agreed to grant a loan of RMB 80 million to Liu Xingwei, but on the condition that Longdong Company first borrow RMB 30 million from Lanzhou Bank in its own name to help Chunyuan Company repay the loans of the 21 fruit farmers, and that Lanzhou Bank would make a loan to Longdong Company after the New Year. Because Longdong Company had no collateral, Liu Xingwei contacted Qin Kunyu, the de facto controller of Huayuan Company, intending to use Huayuan Company's "Huayuan Holiday Tourism Hotel" as a mortgage. Since his wholly-owned company, Teheng Real Estate Company, urgently needed funds for the "Xinhewan" commercial and residential community project developed in Zhenyuan County, Qingyang City, Qin Kunyu, under Xiao Fei's promise of a loan to him, discussed the matter multiple times with Mi Chunhui, Liu Xingwei, Xiao Fei, and others, and reached an oral package agreement: before the end of 2015, Qin Kunyu would provide a mortgage over the real property, Liu Xingwei would borrow RMB 30 million from Lanzhou Bank to repay Mi Chunhui's debt to 21 fruit farmers, and Lanzhou Bank promised to make a loan of RMB 80 million to Liu Xingwei and a loan of RMB 120 million (including the earlier loan of RMB 30 million, totaling RMB 150 million) to Qin Kunyu after the New Year; at the same time, it was agreed that if Qin Kunyu needed to use the same real property for another mortgage loan, Liu Xingwei would immediately repay the loan, release the mortgage, and return the property certificate to Qin Kunyu. Mi Chunhui, on behalf of Chunyuan Company, made a written commitment to Huayuan Company, pledging the company's building and fruit warehouse as security, and promising to pay Liu Xingwei RMB 12 million in cash around the New Year as security for the performance of his obligation to repay, release the mortgage, and return the property certificate. Liu Xingwei simultaneously made a written commitment that if he failed to repay on time, release the mortgage, and return the property certificate, he would guarantee with all his property rights and interests in the contractual operation of the "Huayuan Holiday Tourism Hotel", including the rescission of the operation contract and all his personal property rights and interests such as the RMB 5 million operation fee already paid, RMB 1 million decoration deposit, and initial decoration investments. On December 30, 2015, Longdong Company entered into a loan agreement with Lanzhou Bank, Huayuan Company provided a mortgage over the "Huayuan Holiday Tourism Hotel" as security, and Lanzhou Bank transferred the RMB 30 million loan (with a term of one year) to Chunyuan Company's account, and Chunyuan Company repaid the bank loans of the 21 fruit farmers. Starting in March 2016, Qin Kunyu repeatedly urged Lanzhou Bank to disburse the loan as soon as possible, but was told by Xiao Fei that it could not be processed. Meanwhile, Chunyuan Company failed to fulfill its payment promise and guarantee obligations to Liu Xingwei, and Liu Xingwei also failed to fulfill his commitment to Huayuan Company to promptly return the property certificate. As a result, Qin Kunyu was unable to obtain a loan from Lanzhou Bank, and lacking collateral to obtain financing from other banks, the "Xinhewan" commercial and residential community project came to a complete halt. On August 28, 2017, Lanzhou Bank sued Longdong Company, Huayuan Company, and others in the Qingyang Intermediate People's Court, seeking an order for Longdong Company to repay the loan and to enforce the mortgage over Huayuan Company's real property. Since Longdong Company, as the borrower, did not voluntarily repay the loan, the mortgaged property would inevitably go through a relatively lengthy trial and enforcement process, causing substantial losses. Moreover, in the short term, there was no hope of refinancing with the mortgage. The development project, which had already been suspended for nearly a year and a half, urgently needed funds to resume work due to ongoing incidents of migrant workers demanding payment. Qin Kunyu had no choice but to accept another "rolling over the debt with a new loan" plan proposed by Lanzhou Bank: Teheng Operation Company, controlled by Bian Runmei (Qin Kunyu's mother) and in which Qin Kunyu held an equity interest, would borrow RMB 23 million (with a term of one year) from Lanzhou Bank as the borrower, and Qin Kunyu would self-finance RMB 13,488,949.99, totaling RMB 36,488,949.99, to be paid by Teheng Operation Company on behalf of Longdong Company to settle the principal and interest owed to Lanzhou Bank; Xiao Fei arranged for Haowei Real Estate Company, Ruixinyuan Import and Export Company, Hongda Road and Bridge Company, and their legal representatives Li Ning, Liu Wannian, and Wei Zhenggang to provide joint and several guarantee security for the said loan, and Teheng Real Estate Company, Qin Kunyu, Bian Runmei, and Ding Yiwen (Qin Kunyu's wife) also provided joint and several guarantee security for the said loan; at the same time, Qin Kunyu pledged 100% of his equity in Teheng Real Estate Company valued at RMB 33.6 million, in three equal parts of RMB 11.2 million each, to Haowei Company, Ruixinyuan Company, and Hongda Company as counter-guarantees for the guarantee security provided by those companies for the said loan. Qin Kunyu issued a letter of commitment to Lanzhou Bank stating that "no reporting, accusation, or other means of recourse shall be pursued against Xiao Fei". On September 28, 2017, Teheng Operation Company repaid the amount of RMB 36,488,949.99 owed to Lanzhou Bank on behalf of Longdong Company, and the loan of RMB 23 million from Lanzhou Bank to Teheng Operation Company has been outstanding to date. Xiao Fei's promise of "making a loan after the New Year" as the person in charge of Lanzhou Bank was an act within the scope of his duties, and Lanzhou Bank should bear the responsibility. Lanzhou Bank's false promise, which induced Huayuan Company to enter into the "Mortgage Contract No. Lan Yin Di Zi 2015 Nian Di 101972015000108-4" is a contract concluded by one party's fraud and should be rescinded. Upon rescission of the contract, the corresponding mortgage registration should also be cancelled. After Lanzhou Bank filed the lawsuit on August 28, 2017, the series of contracts entered into by Qin Kunyu with Lanzhou Bank were all concluded under circumstances where he was in a state of distress and against his true intentions. These constitute voidable civil acts and voidable contracts under Article 151 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 54 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as "Contract Law"), and should be rescinded. Due to Lanzhou Bank's fraudulent conduct, the six persons including Huayuan Company were neither able to obtain the promised loan within the agreed time nor able to replace the collateral within the agreed time, forcing the development project to stop and causing substantial losses. According to Article 157 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 58 of the Contract Law, Lanzhou Bank should bear the primary liability for compensation. Although Chunyuan Company and Liu Xingwei each issued corresponding letters of commitment to Qin Kunyu to guarantee Liu Xingwei's timely repayment, they all breached their commitments and failed to perform. Their breach of contract directly prevented the timely release of the mortgage on the "Huayuan Holiday Tourism Hotel", making it impossible for Qin Kunyu to obtain financing loans from other banks, causing the project to stop and resulting in substantial losses. They should be liable for compensation. In summary, pursuant to Article 8 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 128 of the Contract Law, Lanzhou Bank, Liu Xingwei, and Chunyuan Company should bear joint and several liability for compensation.

Because the claims of the six persons including Huayuan Company were complex and numerous, the first-instance court, pursuant to Article 225 of the Judicial Interpretation on Civil Procedure Law, held a pre-trial meeting on September 4, 2018, attended by some of the parties, and requested the six persons including Huayuan Company to clarify their claims. The six persons including Huayuan Company indicated that their claims were divided into two parts: one part consisted of claims for rescission, and the other part consisted of claims for compensation. There were originally five requests for rescission, but they later discovered that the first four claims in the original complaint all pertained to the content of the oral package settlement agreement, so they subsequently added claims. At the same time, they argued that the action actually concerned two oral agreements reached among several parties; on the surface, these appeared to be two separate sets of facts, but the earlier facts and the later facts had a continuing relationship and constituted the same facts.

On September 5, 2018, Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs submitted to the court of first instance an "Explanation on the Claims for Litigation Requests," clarifying the parties for the first nine claims: Claim 1 was made by Teheng Operating Company; Claim 2 was made by Teheng Operating Company to request rescission of the RMB 23 million loan contract, and by Teheng Real Estate Company, Qin Kunyu, Ding Yiwen, and Bian Runmei to request rescission of the guarantee contracts entered into with Lanzhou Bank for this loan, while confirming that after rescission of the above contracts, Teheng Operating Company would return the RMB 23 million loan to Lanzhou Bank; Claim 3 was made by Qin Kunyu; Claim 4 was made by Qin Kunyu; Claim 5 was made by Huayuan Company; Claim 6 was made by Teheng Operating Company; Claim 7 was made by Huayuan Company; Claim 8 was made by Teheng Real Estate Company; Claim 9 was made by Huayuan Company.

The court of first instance, after examination, held that: although Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs claimed that the facts underlying their claims were the same due to continuity and correlation, their claims included rescission of factual acts, rescission of contracts, rescission of registration acts, claims for damages based on contractual acts and factual acts, and claims for assumption of guaranty liability based on contractual acts and factual acts. The litigation claims of Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs were not identical, the legal facts giving rise to them were not entirely the same, the factual bases for seeking to impose obligations on the defendants differed, the types of liabilities to be assumed were not the same, and the subject matter of the litigation was neither common nor of the same type, and the nature of the legal relationships underlying the claims also differed. Therefore, these claims could not be regarded as a single legal relationship integrity or the same fact. Pursuant to Article 52 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the "Civil Procedure Law") and Article 221 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law, this case did not constitute a necessary joint action and should not be consolidated for trial. The consolidated filing by Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs did not meet the statutory conditions for filing a lawsuit. In accordance with Article 119, Article 154(1)(iii) of the Civil Procedure Law, and Article 208(3) of the Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law, the court of first instance ruled as follows: The filing of the lawsuit by Huayuan Company, Teheng Operating Company, Teheng Real Estate Company, Qin Kunyu, Bian Runmei, and Ding Yiwen is dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 1,047,100 prepaid by Huayuan Company and Teheng Real Estate Company shall be refunded.

Opinion of the Court

The issue in dispute in this case is whether the filing of the lawsuit by Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs satisfied the conditions for consolidated trial, and whether the ruling of the court of first instance dismissing their filing was correct.

According to the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and the Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law, lawsuits that may be consolidated for trial include three situations: (1) lawsuits based on the same fact; (2) joint actions where the subject matter of the litigation is common or of the same type; (3) the principal claim and the counterclaim. In this case, to determine whether the filing of the lawsuit by Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs satisfied the conditions for consolidated trial, we must evaluate from two aspects: whether the filing was based on the same fact, and whether it constituted a joint action. The analysis is as follows.

First, the filing of the lawsuit by Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs in this case was not based on the same fact. According to the complaint of Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs, this case involved a series of disputes arising from three related legal relationships. (1) The dispute arising from the loan by Longdong Company from Lanzhou Bank, with Huayuan Company providing real estate mortgage as security: based on this legal relationship, Huayuan Company requested rescission of the mortgage contract and mortgage registration, and requested Liu Xingwei to assume guaranty liability — that is, Claims 5 and 9. (2) The dispute arising from the loan contract entered into by Teheng Operating Company with Lanzhou Bank for the purpose of repaying Longdong Company's debt, and the related guarantee and counter-guarantee contracts: based on this legal relationship, Teheng Operating Company requested rescission of the repayment act and the loan contract, Teheng Real Estate Company, Qin Kunyu, Ding Yiwen, and Bian Runmei requested rescission of the guarantee contracts, Qin Kunyu requested rescission of the relevant pledge contracts and pledge registration, and Qin Kunyu requested rescission of the letter of commitment issued by him — that is, Claims 1, 2, 3, and 4. (3) The dispute arising from the failure of Lanzhou Bank, Chunyuan Company, and Liu Xingwei to fulfill their commitments: Huayuan Company requested that Lanzhou Bank, Chunyuan Company, and Liu Xingwei compensate Huayuan Company for related interest losses, income losses, and project shutdown losses — that is, Claims 6, 7, and 8.

Article 221 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law provides: "Where disputes based on the same fact occur and the parties separately file lawsuits with the same People's Court, the People's Court may consolidate the trials." According to this provision, the lawsuits that may be consolidated for trial should arise "based on the same fact," and the facts or legal relationships on which they are based should be consistent or overlapping. In this case, the filing of the lawsuit by Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs was based on three loan legal relationships successively established by Chunyuan Company, Longdong Company, and Teheng Operating Company with Lanzhou Bank, as well as the mortgage guarantee legal relationships, guarantee legal relationships, and counter-guarantee legal relationships derived from these three loan legal relationships. Among the above legal relationships, Longdong Company borrowed from Lanzhou Bank, and Huayuan Company provided the "Huayuan Holiday Tourist Hotel" as mortgage to guarantee Longdong Company — the mortgage guarantee legal relationship and the loan relationship were connected and could be joined in one action. Teheng Operating Company borrowed from Lanzhou Bank, and Qin Kunyu, Bian Runmei, Ding Yiwen, Teheng Real Estate Company, Haowei Company, Ruixinyuan Company, Hongda Company, Li Ning, Liu Wannian, and Wei Zhenggang provided guarantee for Teheng Operating Company — the guarantee legal relationship and the loan relationship were connected and could be joined in one action. Mi Chunhui, on behalf of Chunyuan Company, made a written commitment to Huayuan Company using the fruit warehouse and building, and Qin Kunyu pledged his 100% equity in Teheng Real Estate Company to Haowei Company, Ruixinyuan Company, and Hongda Company — these constituted counter-guarantee legal relationships, which should be resolved separately by the rights holders after dealing with the guarantee legal relationships. Therefore, it can be seen that the three loan legal relationships involved in this case were not connected, and the litigation claims of Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs were different, and the legal relationships on which the claims were based were also different. Thus, the filing of this lawsuit was not based on the same fact and did not meet the conditions for consolidated trial under the above judicial interpretation.

Second, the filing of the lawsuit by Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs did not constitute a joint action. According to Article 52 of the Civil Procedure Law, joint actions include necessary joint actions and ordinary joint actions. A necessary joint action is an action where the subject matter of the litigation is common, and it is an indivisible action; all co-litigants must participate in the action together; otherwise, the parties are not proper. The three loan legal relationships in this case were independent of each other, constituting independent subject matters of litigation, and there was no connection between the subject matters; they could be sued separately and did not constitute a necessary joint action. An ordinary joint action is an action where the subject matters of the litigation are of the same type, and the People's Court considers that consolidation is appropriate and the parties agree to consolidation. Although the three loan legal relationships involved in this case were of the same type, the subjects involved in each loan legal relationship were different, the guarantee legal relationships were different, and the litigation claims proposed by Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs based on the different legal relationships were different and directed at different subjects. Therefore, this case also did not constitute an ordinary joint action and did not meet the conditions for consolidated trial.

Third, the ruling of the court of first instance dismissing the filing after providing clarification did not violate the right of action of Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs. After inquiry by this court, Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs acknowledged that the court of first instance had informed them that the proposed claims were not suitable for consolidated filing and suggested separate actions. They also indicated that there were four claims that were indeed unsuitable for being brought together in this case and would be withdrawn, but subsequently they did not submit a corresponding application for withdrawal of those claims to the court of first instance. This court holds that, after informing Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs that their filing did not meet the conditions for consolidated trial, and where they did not withdraw the corresponding claims, the court of first instance, based on the actual circumstances of the case and fully protecting the parties' procedural choice, ruled to dismiss the filing on the ground that their filing did not meet the statutory conditions for filing a lawsuit. The finding of facts and application of law were not improper. In the second instance, although Huayuan Company and Qin Kunyu declared that they abandoned Claims 3, 4, 5, and 9, since they did not submit an application for partial withdrawal of claims within a reasonable period after the court of first instance provided clarification, their abandonment of some claims in the second instance does not affect the result of the court of first instance's ruling. Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs may separately file lawsuits based on their claims arising from the same legal relationship; if the filing conditions are met, the People's Court shall accept and hear them in accordance with the law.

In conclusion, the appeal of Huayuan Company and the other five plaintiffs cannot be sustained. The ruling of the court of first instance is clear in fact-finding and correct in application of law. Pursuant to Article 170(1)(i) and Article 171 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original ruling is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
